strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-26699 in numpy: np.linspace with equal infinite endpoints (inf,inf) computes inf-inf in delta, yielding NaN interior points and a spurious RuntimeWarning on the buggy revision b8853b27c188; the fixed revision skips the subtraction for equal endpoints via where= so the step is zero and output is N copies of X with no warning. Target the regression test test_inf_equal_endpoints in numpy/_core/tests/test_function_base.py, which runs under warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning).

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy b8853b27c188 the test FAILS: linspace(inf, inf, num) returns NaN interior values and emits a RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in subtract', which is raised as an error by warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning). On the fixed revision the test PASSES: all equal-infinite-endpoint cases return N copies of X with zero step and no RuntimeWarning. Mixed-infinity test test_inf_mixed_endpoints_warns should still pass on both revisions.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.linspace(np.inf, np.inf, 4) and np.linspace(-np.inf, -np.inf, 4) under warnings as errors

input_output_examples.buggy_output: array([nan, nan, nan, inf]) with RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in subtract

risks: Platform: the defect is a floating-point invalid-operation path; it appears on standard IEEE-754 builds (x86_64, aarch64) with default FP error reporting. It will not reproduce where FP error checking is disabled or the build is wasm (the mixed-endpoint test is skipped on IS_WASM).
Dtype: dtype is not stated in the evidence and is null; the reproducer uses default float64 linspace inputs, which is an assumption.

Discussion vs final diff: the discussion revision used np.errstate(invalid='ignore') with where/zeros_like, but the final diff uses where=; the test checks for absence of warnings, so a fix using errstate suppression would also pass the test but is not the committed approach.
Build: the buggy and fixed revisions are C-extension builds; an editable install must be rebuilt when switching commits, otherwise stale binaries can mask the transition.
Oracle: tolerance, reference source and ulp requirements are not stated; the test uses exact assert_array_equal, so the oracle is exact.
Sanitisers or debug FP traps (e.g. fenv exceptions enabled globally) could change whether the warning is raised; not stated in evidence.
The PR date and python version are not given in the evidence; the buggy commit hash is taken as authoritative.

oracle.reference_source: test_diff assertions against np.full(num, inf) and array([inf, inf])
oracle.why: Expected values are exact infinities and zero step, so exact comparison is appropriate.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On b8853b27c188 linspace(inf, inf, num) computes inf-inf=nan in delta, producing NaN interior points and a RuntimeWarning; under warnings.simplefilter('error', RuntimeWarning) the warning becomes an exception, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision equal endpoints skip the subtraction (where=~equal, zero step), so no warning is raised and assert_array_equal against N copies of inf succeeds.
